summary: Adds three HTTP endpoints. /users searches users by name, /count counts requests per key in memory, and /upstream reports the status code of the upstream service.

findings.title: SQL query built from request input
findings.problem: Search uses fmt.Sprintf to put the name query parameter straight into the SQL text. No escaping or binding happens first.
findings.consequence: Any client can inject SQL through the name parameter. The attacker can then read or change any row the database user can reach.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter. Remove the formatted string.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu before it checks the key. The empty-key branch then returns without unlocking h.mu.
findings.consequence: One request without a key leaves h.mu locked for good. Every later /count request then blocks forever.
findings.fix: Validate the key before calling h.mu.Lock. Another option is to defer h.mu.Unlock right after the lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil, so the deferred call dereferences nil.
findings.consequence: Each unreachable upstream panics fetchStatus. The server then aborts the connection instead of sending the intended 502.
findings.fix: Move the defer below the err check.

findings.title: Upstream request has no timeout
findings.problem: fetchStatus calls http.Get, which uses the default client. The default client has no timeout.
findings.consequence: A slow upstream holds each /upstream request and its goroutine open indefinitely.
findings.fix: Use an http.Client with a Timeout, or a request bound to the incoming request context.

findings.title: New handlers have no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream with new error paths. The repository has no test files that exercise them.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the lock leak and the nil response can ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each new handler, including the error branches.

dropped.reason: This repeats the injection already raised for c1 on the same line.
